stage-000.lore-connecting: Establishing a secure connection to central endpoint. Please wait a few seconds...<pause sec='4'/>
stage-000.lore-endpoint: Endpoint reached, sharing encryption keys... <pause sec='3'/>Done.
stage-001.greeting-new: Welcome! Choose a 4-digit PIN to secure your connection
stage-001.greeting-returning: Welcome back! Re-enter your PIN to decrypt the communication
stage-001.trigram-prompt: Please, enter your Agent Trigram <red>(always reuse the same 3 letters if you have been disconnected)</red>: <input var='Trigram'/><pause sec='2'/>
stage-002.line-01:
Thank you! Now, please wait for agent contact...
<pause sec='5'/>
stage-003.line-02: Hi there! I am Tank, your Operator and I am here to help you.
stage-003.line-03: Please tell me your agent name <red>(limit yourself to a maximum of 24 characters)</red>: <input var='Username'/><pause sec='4'/>
stage-003.line-04: Hi agent <white>{Username}</white>, it's our first time together. Don't be afraid, you are in good hands!<pause sec='2'/>
stage-003.line-05: We do not have too much time, I will guide you during this mission. Please follow my instructions closely.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-004.line-02: <white>{Username}</white>, we have intercepted a message from the vilains and we now have access to their Nutanix cluster.
stage-004.line-03: They don't care about elementary security rules, it is our chance.
stage-006.line-05: We need to act quickly! You are used to this kind of situation... <pause sec='3'/>
stage-006.line-06: First we have to create a new local administrator for this Cluster, in case the vilains change the password. They are sharing passwords using emails, but they probably have a change policy.
stage-006.line-07: Please, connect to the cluster and create a new user <white><copy>{Trigram}-adm</copy></white>. This can be done in the <white>Admin Center</white> part of the GUI.
stage-006.line-08:
<red>Be careful when you login, the </red><white>{PCUser}</white><red> user is a local account!</red>
<image src='stage-006-local-account.png' alt='Nutanix login screen — click the Local Account link to switch.'/>
stage-007.line-01: Now create an <white>Authorization Policy</white> named <white><copy>{Trigram}-auth</copy></white> to give <white>Super Admin</white> rights to <white><copy>{Trigram}-adm</copy></white>.
stage-008.line-02: Now, disconnect from Nutanix Prism Central and connect back with your new user <white><copy>{Trigram}-adm</copy></white>. Hit <white>Enter</white> when you are in.<input/>
stage-009.line-01: I don't have time to check if you are really connected with the account <white>{Trigram}-adm</white>! I trust you this time <white>{Username}</white>, even if the error is (only) human...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-009.line-02: I need you to create a new project. Projects are used to group resources, manage access rights and define quotas. It is the Nutanix way to handle tenants. Users from other projects won't see what we do in our own project.
stage-009.line-03: <red>Oh... Just one important thing!</red> If I forgot to guide you into the right part of the interface, use the <white>search bar</white> at the top of Prism Central UI! It is soooo useful to move quickly from one page to another.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-009.line-04: Let's try it! Type <white>projects</white> in the search bar, then create a new project named <white><copy>{Trigram}-proj</copy></white> with user <white><copy>TheProjectManager</copy></white> as <white>Project Admin</white>.
stage-009.line-05: Finally, after having created the project, go in the <white>Infrastructure</white> tab of this project, add a new infrastructure with our Nutanix cluster and the VLAN/Subnet named <white><copy>{SecondaryNetwork}</copy></white>.
stage-009.line-06: Press <white>Enter</white> when the project is created. <input/>
stage-010.line-02: You know what?<pause sec='1'/> I already feel that we are great teammates!<pause sec='3'/>
stage-010.line-03: Bob has updated switch configuration. You need to create a new subnet in the Nutanix cluster to use it. It should help us to extract data outside without being detected.
stage-010.line-04: Go in the <white>Infrastructure</white> menu and create a new subnet named <white><copy>{Trigram}-subnet</copy></white> with the VLAN ID <white><copy>{Vlanid}</copy></white>.
stage-010.line-05: Subnet can provide IP to VM like a DHCP and that's very useful for us. This is called <white>Nutanix IPAM</white> and please ensure to use it!
stage-010.line-06: Please configure your subnet with these informations:
stage-010.line-12: <red>Important:</red> Uncheck <white>VLAN Basic Networking</white> in the <white>Advanced Configuration</white>.
stage-010.line-13: I am waiting for your feedback. Press <white>Enter</white> when the subnet is setup: <input/>
stage-011.line-02: We are good, especially you.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-011.line-03: Before creating a VM, we need to add an image in the library. I pushed a home-made image on the ubuntu official repository. It should be enough to fake the others.
stage-011.line-04: Add a disk image named <white><copy>{Trigram}-ubuntu</copy></white> in the image library from this <white>URL</white>:
stage-011.line-06: <red>Warning:</red> Please ensure the image is a <white>disk</white> image, <red>not</red> an <white>ISO</white> image.
stage-011.line-07: Press <white>Enter</white> when the image is available on the cluster: <input/>
stage-012.line-02: We are on time and that is good, but we need to hurry up. I have detected an activity from the others... they are looking for us. We need to work carefully.
stage-012.line-03: Please, create a new VM named <white><copy>{Trigram}-vm</copy></white> with the following configuration:
stage-012.line-06: - <white>20GB</white> disk based on the <white><copy>{Trigram}-ubuntu</copy></white> image we just uploaded
stage-012.line-09:
You can use this <white>cloud-init</white> to create a few users in this VM:
<pause sec='1'/>
stage-012.line-10: #cloud-config users: - name: nutanix shell: /bin/bash sudo: ['ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'] - name: admin shell: /bin/bash sudo: ['ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'] primary_group: users groups: [sudo] no_user_group: true chpasswd: list: | nutanix:MyPassword admin:MyPassword expire: false ssh_pwauth: true write_files: - path: /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml permissions: '0600' content: | network: version: 2 ethernets: all-eths: match: name: "e*" dhcp4: true runcmd: - netplan apply
stage-012.line-11: After that, use the <white>Manage Ownership</white> action in the VM contextual menu to move it into your project and set <white><copy>TheProjectManager</copy></white> as the owner.
stage-012.line-12:
<yellow><bold>Start the VM!</bold></yellow> Wait until it is powered on before continuing.

Then press <white>Enter</white>: <input/>
stage-013.line-02: I am not very peaceful, there are many strange things happening around us.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-013.line-03: Please, disconnect from Nutanix Prism Central and connect back with the <red>Active Directory</red> user <white><copy>{ProdUsername}</copy></white> using password <white><copy>{ProdPassword}</copy></white> ...
stage-013.line-04: Then look at the VM list in the UI, and confirm the VM you have created is not listed.
stage-014.line-02: Perfect, it is pretty discrete. The user <white><copy>{ProdUsername}</copy></white> owns to <white><copy>Production</copy></white> project only. He is not able to see assets from others projects. So, they won't see your VM, except if they look for it. We need to be careful.
stage-014.line-03: Please, connect back with our admin user <white><copy>{Trigram}-adm</copy></white> on Nutanix Prism Central and hit <white>Enter</white> when you are ready.<input/>
stage-014.line-04: <pause sec='6'/>Oh wait!!!<pause sec='2'/> They are scanning the server hosting our VM. Whoopsie-daisy!
stage-014.line-05: Move our VM to another one right now! <red>I recommend you to first click on the VM and check the node it is running on and then migrate it to another node.</red>
stage-015.line-02: Thanks god, they have not detected the VM... Wooow, it was very hot!
stage-015.line-03: Now we are starting serious things. Unfortunately, you are not Nutanix certified, but it is not a big deal. Nutanix makes things simple with their interface and you should easily find how to do things by yourself.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-015.line-04: In the <white>Admin Center</white> page, you should find something to manage categories. Nutanix uses Categories to manage all the policies on the cluster, it is very efficient.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-015.line-05: Create a new category <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat</copy></white> with 2 values : <white><copy>Critical</copy></white> and <white><copy>Test</copy></white>.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-015.line-06: I am waiting for your feedback ... press <white>Enter</white> when it's done: <input/>
stage-015.line-08: Nice, you work quickly. I expect you didn't do it dirty... <pause sec='4'/>
stage-016.line-01: Can you go back in the <white>Infrastructure</white> page on your VM view and apply the category <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat</copy></white> with value <white><copy>Critical</copy></white> to it please?
stage-017.line-02: Now we are going to create different policies to protect our VM and first we are going to encrypt it!<pause sec='3'/>
stage-017.line-03: For that, you need to create a Storage policy <white><copy>{Trigram}-sto-policy</copy></white> enabling the encryption. You can use the default values for the other fields cause we do not really care about them here, but if you are curious, take a look at them, it is interesting.
stage-017.line-04: Apply it to VMs with your category <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat</copy></white> and the value <white><copy>Critical</copy></white>.
stage-018.line-02: Let's protect our VM. Microsegmentation controls which traffic can reach it and which traffic can leave.
stage-018.line-03: The villains left their doors open. We won't make the same mistake.
stage-018.line-04: Create a Security policy named <white><copy>{Trigram}-mseg-policy</copy></white> with these settings:
stage-018.line-06: - Policy Hitlogs: <white>Enabled</white> so we can observe the blocked traffic
stage-018.line-07: - <white>Deny all incoming traffic</white> to the VM
stage-018.line-08: - Apply it to your category <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat</copy></white> with value <white><copy>Critical</copy></white>
stage-018.help-01: Step 1 · Define Policy. Follow the numbers on the screenshot: name the policy (1), choose Application: Secure Entities (2), set Policy Hitlogs to Enabled (3), then click Next (4). Policy name:{Trigram}-mseg-policy
stage-018.help-02: <white>Step 2 · Secure Application.</white> Click <white>Add Secured Entity</white> in the middle column.<image src='stage-018-step-02.png' alt='Secure Application'/>
stage-018.help-03: <white>Step 3 · Add Entity.</white> Entity: <white>VM</white> (1). Category: your category <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat:Critical</copy></white> (2). Then click <white>Apply</white> (3).<image src='stage-018-step-03.png' alt='Add Entity'/>
stage-018.help-04: <white>Step 4 · Check the result.</white> Your category is listed under <white>Secured Entities</white>, and the <white>Outbounds</white> switch to <white>Allow All</white> on their own: nothing to do there. The <white>Inbounds</white> stay on <white>Deny all incoming traffic</white>, as intended for now. Click <white>Next</white>.<image src='stage-018-step-04.png' alt='Secured Entities and Outbounds'/>
stage-018.help-05: <white>Step 5 · Review.</white> Select <white>Apply (Enforce)</white> (1), not Monitor, then click <white>Confirm</white> (2). Come back here and press <white>Enter</white>.<image src='stage-018-step-05.png' alt='Review'/>
stage-018.help-06: <dim>If validation fails: check the exact policy name, Application type, Enforce mode, Policy Hitlogs enabled, and VM category {Trigram}-cat:Critical. Block all inbound traffic and allow all outbound traffic.</dim>
stage-019.line-02: Let's test our defenses. Open the SSH console in a new tab. Find the IP of {Trigram}-vm on its Prism page.
stage-019.line-03: Run <white>ping <your vm ip></white>, then <white>ssh admin@<your vm ip></white>. Both attempts should fail.<pause sec='15'/>
stage-019.line-04: Open <white>{Trigram}-mseg-policy</white> and look for traffic from <white>{frontendHost}</white> under <white>Blocked</white>: ICMP and TCP port 22. Nothing yet? Wait a moment and try again; check <white>Show Discovered Traffic</white> is enabled.
stage-019.line-05: Those are our attempts. Now let us back in, without opening every door.
stage-019.line-06: Click <white>Update</white>, then <white>Next</white>. Create these two separate inbound rules:
stage-019.line-07: - From the blocked source <white>{frontendHost}/32</white>, choose <white>Allow</white> and select only <white>TCP 22</white> (SSH). Leave ICMP unselected.
stage-019.line-08:
- Add a new inbound source: <white>Allow All</white>.
 - Connect it to your secured category. Choose <white>Allow Specific Traffic</white>.
 - Add <white>ICMPv4</white>, with Type <white>8</white> and Code <white>0</white>.

Keep all other inbound traffic blocked.
stage-019.line-09: Apply the policy in <white>Enforce</white> mode. Test ping and SSH again from the console: both should now succeed. Then press <white>Enter</white>: <input/>
stage-019.line-11: I'll check the rules. The traffic observations are yours.
stage-019.help-01: Step 1 · Test the block. In the SSH console: Run ping <your vm ip>, then ssh admin@<your vm ip>. Both attempts should fail.
stage-019.help-02: <white>Step 2 · Open the editor.</white> Open <white>{Trigram}-mseg-policy</white>, click <white>Update</white>, then <white>Next</white> to reach <white>Secure Application</white>.<image src='stage-019-step-01.png' alt='Security policy'/>
stage-019.help-03: <white>Step 3 · Use the blocked source.</white> Under <white>Inbounds → Blocked</white>, find <white>{frontendHost}/32</white> (1). Open its <white>⋮</white> menu and choose <white>Allow</white> (2). The screenshot uses example addresses; select the game IP shown here.<image src='stage-019-discovered-allow.png' alt='Blocked traffic'/>
stage-019.help-04: <white>Step 4 · Allow SSH only.</white> Select only the <white>TCP 22</white> row (1). Leave <white>ICMP 8,0</white> unchecked; no service mapping is needed. Click <white>Allow 1 Discovered Traffic</white> (2). This creates the SSH rule from the game IP /32.<image src='stage-019-discovered-ssh.png' alt='TCP 22'/>
stage-019.help-05: <white>Step 5 · Add the ICMP source.</white> In <white>Inbounds</white>, click <white>Add Source</white>. Choose <white>Allow All</white> as the entity (1), then <white>Apply</white> (2). This defines the source, not the allowed protocols.<image src='stage-019-icmp-source.png' alt='Allow All'/>
stage-019.help-06: <white>Step 6 · Connect the source.</white> Select the new inbound <white>Allow All</white> card (1), then click the <white>+</white> on the left edge of your secured VM/category card (2).<image src='stage-019-icmp-connect.png' alt='Inbound rule'/>
stage-019.help-07: <white>Step 7 · Limit the traffic.</white> Set <white>Traffic Filtering</white> to <white>Allow Specific Traffic</white> (1). Open <white>Add New Protocol-Port / Service</white> (2), then select <white>ICMPv4</white> (3).<image src='stage-019-icmp-filter.png' alt='Allow Specific Traffic'/>
stage-019.help-08: <white>Step 8 · Allow Echo Request.</white> Enter Type <white>8</white> (1) and Code <white>0</white> (2), then click <white>Save</white> (3). Do not add SSH to this rule.<image src='stage-019-icmp-echo.png' alt='ICMPv4: 8 / 0'/>
stage-019.help-09: <white>Step 9 · Review both rules.</white> Switch to <white>List</white>. Check two inbound rules: <white>{frontendHost}/32 → TCP 22</white> and <white>Allow All → ICMPv4 Type 8 Code 0</white>. Both target <white>{Trigram}-cat:Critical</white>. Keep outbound Allow All, then click <white>Next</white>.<image src='stage-019-two-rules.png' alt='TCP 22 / ICMPv4'/>
stage-019.help-10: <white>Step 10 · Enforce.</white> Keep <white>Apply (Enforce)</white> selected (1), then click <white>Confirm</white> (2).<image src='stage-019-enforce.png' alt='Apply (Enforce)'/>
stage-019.help-11: <white>Step 11 · Test again.</white> Run ping and SSH again from the game console. Ping should answer and SSH should reach port 22. Return here and press <white>Enter</white>.
stage-019.help-12: <white>Step 12 · If something is missing.</white> No blocked traffic? Wait briefly, retry both probes, and check <white>Show Discovered Traffic</white>, Policy Hitlogs, the VM power state and its category. Validation checks the policy configuration, not the discovered traffic. SSH must use the game IP /32; ICMP 8/0 must use Allow All.
stage-020.line-02: We have a last policy to setup: a protection policy. It is a way to pilot snapshots and their replication, to reduce disaster impact.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-020.line-03: Create a new Protection policy named <white><copy>{Trigram}-prot-policy</copy></white> with the following properties:
stage-020.line-04: - No need to replicate, so <white>no need for a Recovery Location</white>
stage-020.line-05: - Just a <white>local schedule</white>, with the below settings:
stage-020.line-08: . Set snapshot retention to <white>Daily</white>, with a frequency of <white>1</white>.
stage-020.line-09: - Applied to VM with your categorie <white><copy>{Trigram}-cat</copy></white> and value <white><copy>Critical</copy></white>.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-021.line-01: To secure our work, we are going to setup an approval policy for snapshot deletion. It will avoid any deletion of our snapshots by our... embarrassing friends!
stage-021.line-02: For that, we must create an <white>approval policy</white> with the below settings:<pause sec='3'/>
stage-021.line-05: - 3 approvers in this set : <white><copy transform='lowercase'>Charlie</copy></white>, <white><copy transform='lowercase'>Thom</copy></white> and <white><copy transform='lowercase'>William</copy></white> <red>(add them with lowercase names)</red>.
stage-021.line-07: <red>Warning: this policy may already exist and only one approval policy is allowed. In this case, simply link it to your protection policy as described below.</red>.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-021.line-08: Then associate your protection policy <white><copy>{Trigram}-prot-policy</copy></white> to the existing or created approval policy.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-022.line-01: To be sure the recovery points are protected, just look back at the protection policy page, and ensure your policy has a <white>Secure</white> mention.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-023.line-02: Oh oh... <pause sec='3'/>Don't move please!<pause sec='5'/><action name='deleteVM'/>
stage-023.line-03: Seems that they are inspecting the cluster... Do not do anything. I'm closing the connection to reconnect with a more securized protocol. Wait here, please!
stage-024.line-05: Establishing connection to the endpoint with multi-layer encryption and multiple hops to reduce tracking capabilities...<pause sec='3'/> Connected successfully!
stage-025.line-01: Ok, I'm back. I hope you are still there and in good shape, buddy!
stage-025.line-03: We make a great team <white>{Username}</white>!<pause sec='3'/> We have a job to finish, let's get back to it!<pause sec='5'/>
stage-026.line-03: I can't believe it... but it looks like they have deleted our VM! Fortunately, we still have available recovery points.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-026.line-04: <red>Clone</red> the VM from the latest recovery point available, using its original name <white><copy>{Trigram}-vm</copy></white> as before! Then start it.
stage-026.line-05: I will update myself in the meantime. Note that the <white>Clone</white> operation is no more that a <red>restore</red> process of the VM!
stage-027.line-02: You know what? Since we have a bit of time, let's spy on them. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-027.line-03: Send to this discreet address <white><copy>{Trigram}{EmailReport}</copy></white> a report with the <white>list of VMs</white>, <white>every day at 03:00 AM</white>. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-027.line-04: Reports are managed in the <white>Intelligent Operations</white> part of the GUI. Name it <white><copy>{Trigram}-report</copy></white>. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-028.line-02: Now I need you go on the <white>Infrastructure > Hardware > Clusters</white> page. Then simulate cluster expansion, <red>without validating it</red>!
stage-028.line-03: Just take a screenshot of the review page, it will be useful for a future mission. I can't tell you more right know. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-028.line-04: Please give me <white>the serial number</white> of the new node : <input var='NodeSerial'/>
stage-029.line-01: Let's see how up to date this platform is.
stage-029.line-02: Open <white>Admin Center > LCM</white>. It brings together the available <white>software and firmware updates</white> for the platform.
stage-029.line-03: Take a look at the available upgrades. A little mental math won't hurt. Leave inventory and updates for another day.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-029.line-04: Tell me how many <white>software and firmware updates</white> are available <white>in total</white>: <input var='NumberUpdates'/>
stage-030.line-01: Awesome!<pause sec='2'/> There is one last check to do...<pause sec='1'/>
stage-030.line-02: From the <white>Dashboard</white> page of the <white>Infrastructure</white>, you should have a tile with security concerns.
stage-030.line-03: From here, display the full security Dashboard. and dig into it. Take some screenshot which will help us for upcoming operations.
stage-030.line-04: We will have to act quickly, this tool is very helpfull to identify all security issues of the platform and they probably take care of it. <pause sec='5'/>
stage-031.line-03: We have intercepted a new account for another cluster. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-031.line-04: Not a big catch, it seems to be the account of the person who monitors clusters capacity and node procurement.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-031.line-05: Can you connect on this cluster now, check runway values and give me the number of days remaining on this cluster?<pause sec='3'/>
stage-031.line-06: Required informations to connect are below:
stage-031.line-10: You should find info in the <white>Intelligent Operations</white> page. Just send the <white>number of days</white> here when you have it <red>(only numbers, nothing else)</red>: <input var='Runway'/>
stage-032.line-01: Nutanix provides advices to optimize VM size and reduce the footprint on the cluster. They will probably use it to reduce the cost of the platform and push back the node procurement. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-032.line-02: Take a look at the resources we could reclaim. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-032.line-03: In <white>Intelligent Operations</white>, click the cluster name under <white>Cluster Runway</white>. In its <white>Capacity</white> view, open <white>Optimize Resources</white>. Take a screenshot of the potential savings for later; it will help us estimate when they might need more nodes.
stage-033.line-03: Ok! <pause sec='3'/>Now go back on the first cluster please.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-033.line-04: We are going to leverage <white>Intelligent Operations Low-Code</white> capabilities from <white>NCM</white>. They also call this feature <white>X-Play</white> and it is very useful to automate tasks. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-033.line-05: Can you create a new playbook with the below settings:
stage-033.line-07: - Actions: Send an email to <white><copy>{Trigram}{EmailReport}</copy></white> as soon as a an event happens about a VM that is <white>Power Cycled</white>.
stage-033.line-08: - Details: In the email body, put the <white>VM ID</white> please.
stage-033.line-09: <red>And do not forget to enable it!</red>
stage-033.help-01: <white>Step 1 · Open Playbooks.</white> Make sure you are on the <white>first</white> cluster, not the one used in the previous stages. In Prism, open <white>Intelligent Operations</white> then <white>Playbooks</white> (typing <white>Playbooks</white> in the search bar works too), and click <white>Create Playbook</white>.<image src='stage-033-step-01.png' alt='Playbooks'/>
stage-033.help-02: <white>Step 2 · Trigger.</white> Choose <white>Event</white>.<image src='stage-033-step-02.png' alt='Select a Trigger'/>
stage-033.help-03: <white>Step 3 · Event type.</white> Event type: <white>Power cycled VM</white> (1). Then click <white>Add Action</white> (2).<image src='stage-033-step-03.png' alt='Event'/>
stage-033.help-04: <white>Step 4 · Action.</white> Choose <white>Email</white>.<image src='stage-033-step-04.png' alt='Select an Action'/>
stage-033.help-05: Step 5 · The email. Recipient (1):{Trigram}{EmailReport}Subject (2): Choose a subject for the email. Message (3): Include the VM ID. Click Parameters below the field and insert Event: Source Entity UUID. Click Save & Close (4). The blue SMTP banner is informational.
stage-033.help-06: Step 6 · Name it and enable it. Name (1):{Trigram}-playbookMake sure Playbook Status is Enabled (2), then click Save (3). Come back here and press Enter.
stage-033.help-07: <dim>If the check fails: the name must be exactly <white><copy>{Trigram}-playbook</copy></white>, there must be exactly one trigger (VM power cycled) and exactly one action (email), and the playbook must be enabled.</dim>
stage-034.line-01: I think we need to do a test. Can you <white>Power Cycle</white> the VM <white><copy>{Trigram}-vm</copy></white> and then verify the playbook has been played? <pause sec='2'/>
stage-034.line-02: If my informations are accurates, in the playbook page, you have a <white>Plays</white> tab with the execution history.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-034.line-03: Do not hesitate to look at the details of the last execution and verify that the body of the sent email is compliant.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-035.line-03: Let's continue to trap this cluster... <pause sec='3'/>
stage-035.line-04: It seems they are using <white>Nutanix Self-Service</white> to create automation and provide applications in a marketplace for their end-users. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-035.line-05: They have a blueprint to clone some VM into a dedicated network, a.k.a. <white>a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)</white>, for testing purpose obviously. It could be interesting to execute it and I'll be quiet to investigate, not in production and far from potential trackers.
stage-035.line-14: - Category for floating IP: <white><copy>Quarantine</copy></white> (in fact, we don't care about it cause we won't use it)
stage-036.line-01: To have an exact copy of the production VM on a daily basis, I would like you schedule an action named <white>Refresh VM</white>.
stage-036.line-02: It can be done in the <white>Self-Service > Policies</white> page. Name it <white><copy>{Trigram}-sched</copy></white> please.
stage-036.line-03: For your information, your app is currently deployed in the <white><copy>production</copy></white> project. Do a daily task, time does not matter. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-037.line-01: <action name='deployBlueprint'/>Its time for our last task. <pause sec='2'/>We are going to modifiy one of their blueprint, to add a backdoor in the VM they will deploy.
stage-037.line-02: This blueprint is used by their end-users to deploy a new VM in their environment (IPAM, CMDB, DNS, Firewall, Backup, etc).<pause sec='3'/>
